input_latex: x' = - x - 2 y,\qquad y' = 2 x - y
normal_latex: x' = - x - 2 y,\qquad y' = 2 x - y
summary: Linear system. The origin is a spiral sink: asymptotically stable.

methods.name: Eigenvalue method
methods.reason: The system is linear with constant coefficients.

steps.title: Find the eigenvalues
steps.text: Solutions of the form \(\mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t}\) need \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

steps.title: Find a complex eigenvector
steps.text: For \(\lambda = \alpha + \beta i\), split the eigenvector into real and imaginary parts, \(\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{p} + i\mathbf{q}\).

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: The real and imaginary parts of the complex solution are two independent real solutions.
latex: \mathbf{X} = e^{\alpha t}\left[C_1(\mathbf{p}\cos\beta t - \mathbf{q}\sin\beta t) + C_2(\mathbf{p}\sin\beta t + \mathbf{q}\cos\beta t)\right]
x(t) = \left(- C_{1} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + C_{2} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{- t},\qquad y(t) = \left(C_{1} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + C_{2} \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{- t}

steps.title: Apply the initial conditions
steps.text: Set \(t = 0\) and solve the equations for the constants.
latex: x(t) = - e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\qquad y(t) = e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}

steps.title: Classify the equilibrium
steps.text: From the eigenvalues, the origin is a spiral sink: asymptotically stable.

steps.title: Solution
latex: x(t) = - e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\qquad y(t) = e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked by substituting back into every equation, and it meets the initial conditions.

methods.name: Matrix exponential
methods.reason: For a constant matrix the solution is the matrix exponential applied to the initial vector.

steps.title: Use the matrix exponential
steps.text: Just as \(x' = ax\) has solution \(x = e^{at}x(0)\), the system \(\mathbf{X}' = A\mathbf{X}\) has solution \(\mathbf{X} = e^{At}\mathbf{X}(0)\).

steps.title: Compute the exponential
steps.text: Summing the series (in practice through the eigenvalues of \(A\)) gives
latex: e^{At} = \begin{pmatrix}e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} & - e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\\e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} & e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\end{pmatrix}

steps.title: Multiply by the initial vector
latex: x(t) = C_{1} e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} - C_{2} e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)},\qquad y(t) = C_{1} e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + C_{2} e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}

steps.title: Insert the initial values
latex: x(t) = - e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\qquad y(t) = e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}

steps.title: Solution
latex: x(t) = - e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\qquad y(t) = e^{- t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + e^{- t} \cos{\left(2 t \right)}

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked by substituting back into every equation, and it meets the initial conditions.
